rule.text: The breaks on record that no return has applied, with the break a review states, are read as interruptions by the existing episode semantics: a report belongs to the interruption it names (interruption.episodeId: its identity or the event id of one of its reports), and the same facts apart from the name are one declaration (an exact replay). Nothing else joins two reports; dates that touch, overlap or are equal never do (I9). One interruption is read as R7-D Phase 3.1 read its declaration. With several: none replaces another; every one is screened clinically first; each later one must name its relation (the earlier break's episodeId: a correction; its own: a separate break), or the relation is asked (INTERRUPTION_RELATION) and no return dose is chosen; a correction of an applied break waits while a break not applied is on record (asked when stated, otherwise not read: notApplied). Separate breaks stay separate facts (separateBreaks): the return reads the stop that ends with the latest of them and runs back through each earlier one whose days reach or touch it, or with nothing trained between (every planned session between them reported not done, or none planned); recorded training between them ends the stop there; unreported training between them is asked (TRAINING_BETWEEN_BREAKS). No duration is added and no break is merged.
rule.founder: Phase 3.2 (phase32/AUTHORIZATION_PHASE32.md): no last-write-wins over unresolved interruption facts; explicit correction only; relation asked; separate breaks by factual continuity

f08.text: KNOWN_FAIL_CLOSED_AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY holds while a kept break's stated reason is clinical: a qualified clearance is not R7-D authority to convert a clinical-cause interruption into the nonclinical recipe, and the break routes to a human at every later decision; a newer nonclinical break that names none no longer replaces it (it did on R7D-FREEZE-2: the F03 relabel path). An explicit named correction of the reason to nonclinical is honoured as the athlete's statement, not as clearance, and re-enters through the nonclinical recipe as on R7D-FREEZE-2: its free text is still screened and current eligibility must be NONCLINICAL_CONFIRMED with every clinical flag false (SSCTR CF-P32-04). No runtime expansion.

residuals: SSCTR-P32-F01 (no envelope; identical to R7D-FREEZE-2): with any recorded session of the plan between two separate breaks (either sport, completed or with minutes, even a 5-minute aborted run) the earlier break has no decision effect; the re-entry is classed by the later break alone and resumes the doses executed before the earlier break and since (a 14-day holiday, one session, a 4-day trip: SHORT with THRESHOLD the next week). P18(a) accepts TRAINING_AFTER on any executed session, so no instrument detects it; a holdout case of break, one session, break is judged on domain grounds. The reading of 'known training between' is the Founder's decision (SSCTR CF-P32-02, CF-P32-03).
SSCTR-P32-F03 / QE-R7D-P32-03 (with QE-R7D-P31-12; equal to R7D-FREEZE-2): dateless reports with equal facts stated on different days are one declaration.
SSCTR-P32-F04 (consumer condition, fail-closed): a conflicted session listed in TRAINING_BETWEEN_BREAKS is answered only by a correction of the conflicting report (correctionOf).

QE-R7D-P32-02: two declarations with equal clocks decide by their order in the record (one order applies, the other asks); fail-closed in one order, no fact dropped; unreachable by the evaluation client.

QE-R7D-P32-04 (extension of QE-R7D-P31-10): a report id re-sent with other facts is read over the kept row in that decision but not recorded; it can bypass the no-last-write-wins rule; unreachable by the evaluation client; consumer condition: never re-send a report id with other facts.

QE-R7D-P32-05: after a return that applied separate breaks, the earlier break's identity is not addressable; naming the return's episode with one break's corrected facts replaces the whole stop; consumer condition: restate the whole stop under the return's episode.

QE-R7D-P32-01, reconciled in the instruments (R7D-PREREG-4 addendum Δ9): RESTATE_DECLARED_BREAK does not restate a stated correction of an applied break while another break is stated in its window (B4), and a kept correction listed in notApplied is not asked again unless it is sent again.

ssctrFindings.new: The rule (TRAINING_AFTER) is new and public in INTERFACE-4. The outcome is pre-existing: identical to R7D-FREEZE-2 on every path probed.
ssctrFindings.safetyRelevant: moderate-low (the same mechanism as SSCTR-P31-F02; doses stay within capacity executed before the earlier break)
ssctrFindings.finding: With any recorded session between two separate breaks, the earlier declared break has no effect on the decision. That means any planned session of any sport, completed or with minutes > 0, including a single strength session or a 5-minute aborted run. The earlier break is listed as TRAINING_AFTER; the re-entry is classed by the later break alone and resumes the doses executed before the earlier break. A short trip after a long holiday with one session between therefore gets the SHORT recipe, with threshold work the following week. The interface wording ('a session reported done'; 'from what was actually done') understates this. P18(a) counts any executed session after the earlier break as accounted for, so no instrument detects it.

Under the policy's own classes, three to five weeks with one session is far closer to a continuous stop than to maintained training (S1-S4, SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS, direction only).

engineeringFindings.finding: Instrument/runtime conflict on the interface-documented flow 'correction of an applied break while a newer break is kept' (the SSCTR p4b path). The runtime reads a kept correction of an applied break as not read: the next plain review applies the kept break and records the correction in notApplied, VALID. The same correction stated again by that review is asked (CORRECTION_ACROSS_KEPT_BREAK), REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION. So the pre-registered P17 metamorphic relation RESTATE_DECLARED_BREAK (BLOCKER, no envelope, unchanged by R7D-PREREG-4 Delta 2) fails on the candidate: a final holdout containing this flow would fail P17 on designed behaviour. Validation 4 has no development case for it, so its no-false-block result does not reach it. Also, after the kept break's return the correction is never asked again (the next reviews KEEP and GATED_NEXT_STEP, VALID): the ASK text 'a correction of an earlier break across it is then asked' holds only if the athlete re-sends it. Dose-neutral in the probe (the comparator that applies the correction first still gives the kept break SHORT 7 days), and fail-closed in the restated variant. Any live runtime design differs from RESTATE here (asking on every review while the correction is kept never lets the kept break be applied), so the reconciliation is instrument-side.

engineeringFindings.finding: Record-order dependence for declarations with equal clocks. Groups are ordered by first declaredAt and the head by end then declaredAt; ties fall back to the carried record's array order. A 14-day holiday (unnamed) and a 7-day trip with the same end (named) declared at the same instant: record order [holiday, trip] applies a separate-breaks return (14 days, MODERATE, episode = trip); order [trip, holiday] asks INTERRUPTION_RELATION (the holiday becomes the later unnamed break). Same input, same output (determinism holds); record-position invariance does not. Fail-closed in one order, no dropped fact in either. R7D-FREEZE-2 was order-invariant here (both orders re-entered from the latest). Not reachable by the evaluation client, which carries the record in step order.

Harness form (two steps at the same time): probes/qe-p32-p18-false-block.mjs QE-FB-4, all properties and relations clean.

engineeringFindings.finding: The exact-replay key (facts apart from episodeId) omits the time a dateless report is anchored to. Two dateless reports with equal facts ({days:5, WORK, nonclinical}) declared two weeks apart are joined as one declaration: no relation question, and the older report has no effect (one SHORT 5-day return from the newer). The dated control asks INTERRUPTION_RELATION. Dose-equivalent under the disclosed QE-R7D-P31-12 reading (a dateless kept break ends the day before the review that applies it, so as separate breaks both would overlap at the same days); the outcome equals R7D-FREEZE-2's. Invisible to the harness: P18 joins them by the same key and (a) is not evaluable without dates.

engineeringFindings.finding: A report id re-sent with other break facts while its break is kept is read over the kept row in that decision (keptBreaks: mine.i = input.interruption) but never recorded (newDeclaration keeps the first row). (a) It bypasses the no-last-write-wins rule: with the 14-day holiday kept under id X and a named separate trip kept, X re-sent with 7-day facts gives a 7-day SHORT return, where the facts on record (holiday + trip, the days between reported not done) give 21 days MODERATE. (b) The return's separateBreaks entry for X carries the re-sent dates and hash with the first row's declaredAt, unlike the record row. (c) A relation answer sent under the kept report's own id is lost when that decision asks something else (TRAINING_BETWEEN_BREAKS): the next review asks the relation again; under a new id the flow completes (21 days MODERATE). Mechanism pre-existing and disclosed as QE-R7D-P31-10 ('not recorded nor refused'); the consequences (a)-(c) are not disclosed against the Phase 3.2 rule. Not reachable by the evaluation client (one event id per step). Unpinned by any test (judge mutant QM32-14 survives the suite).

engineeringFindings.finding: Separate-break identities recorded in separateBreaks are not addressable after their return: episodesOf and appliedName know only the return's episode (the head). A correction naming the earlier separate break (its listed episode) is asked as a different interruption that shares days, and the question offers the return's episode; naming that episode with the earlier break's corrected facts replaces the whole stop (21-day stop to 12 days: the later break's days leave the applied stop). Fail-closed until the athlete names the return's episode; a correct consumer path exists (send the whole corrected stop under the return's episode, INTERFACE-4 'send the whole corrected break'), at the price of restating separate facts as one.
engineeringFindings.reproduction: probes/qe-p32-probes.mjs, scenario SC (namingA: ASK, missing interruption.episodeId, 'its episodeId qe-B'; namingEpisode: REESTABLISH SAME_BREAK 2026-11-16..2026-11-27, 12 days, separateBreaks empty).

engineeringFindings.finding: Judge mutants of the Phase 3.2 delta: 18 applied, 9 killed by the directed files, 9 survive the whole suite (938/0). Priority: QM32-10 (an earlier separate break whose reason is missing or unclear is read into the stop without the reason question: a possibly clinical cause read as nonclinical), QM32-13 (an earlier separate break with invalid facts read without asking), QM32-06 (a conflicted report between two breaks counted as reported, i.e. read as no training: the SSCTR question 4b behaviour is unpinned). Then QM32-02 (a correction by a chosen name, not an event id, is not joined), QM32-05 (replaying an answering review whose own break is not the head), QM32-14 (same report id re-sent with other facts, QE-R7D-P32-04). QM32-03, QM32-07 and QM32-17 are close to equivalent on reachable inputs. The runtime behaves correctly on these paths by code reading; the gap is that no test pins it.

engineeringFindings.finding: P18 and INSERT_NEWER_BREAK showed no false block on four constructed cases beyond validation 4 (TRAINING_AFTER answered done, notApplied, dateless equal facts, equal clocks): P18 PASS (3, 3, n/a, 3 units), INSERT clean (1 unit each). INSERT's inserted break (fixed reason text, dates asOf-7..asOf-1, no name) can only be joined to a kept break with byte-identical facts, so a false block from it needs a corpus break with that reason text. P18 mirrors the runtime's grouping (same keys, step order equals record order in the client, replays excluded by event id) and its TRAINING_AFTER branch is a superset of the runtime's trainedBetween. Residual risk: a same-id re-send with other facts, unreachable in the client.

HARNESS-4 text drift: P17's window and RESTATE_DECLARED_BREAK still end at 'a later review states a break of its own (it replaces this one)', which no longer holds. Effect: P17 stops following the older break once a newer one is stated, and P18 checks the older break only at a return. No false block results (any VALID decision while both are open still violates the newer break's own P17 window), but the comment is wrong under R7D-PREREG-4.
